questions.text: What is the purpose of the 'self' keyword in a Python class method?
options: To return the method's result
To pass an argument to the method
To refer to the current instance of the class
To end the method's execution
questions.explanation: The 'self' keyword allows the method to access and modify its own attributes and other methods, enabling encapsulation.

questions.text: What is encapsulation in the context of object-oriented programming?
options: Hiding data and behavior from the outside world
Exposing data and behavior to the outside world
Allowing multiple classes to inherit from a parent class
Revealing an object's internal state through its methods
questions.explanation: Encapsulation is the concept of bundling data and behavior together within a single unit (an object or class), controlling access to it, and hiding internal implementation details from the outside world.

questions.text: What does the 'classmethod' decorator do in a Python class method?
options: To make a static method
To make a class method
To make a private method
To make a public method
questions.explanation: The 'classmethod' decorator allows a method to be called on the class itself, rather than an instance of the class.

questions.text: What is inheritance in the context of object-oriented programming?
options: A way to reuse code by creating a new class that builds upon an existing class
A way to create a new class that is completely unrelated to an existing class
A way to change the behavior of an existing class
A way to delete an existing class
questions.explanation: Inheritance is a mechanism that allows a new class to inherit the properties and behavior of an existing class.

questions.text: What does the 'super()' function do in Python?
options: To access the parent class's attributes
To call the parent class's methods
To create a new instance of the parent class
To return the current instance's attributes
questions.explanation: The 'super()' function returns a proxy object that allows calls to methods of a parent class, making it useful for implementing inheritance and polymorphism.

questions.text: What is the difference between a class variable and an instance variable in Python?
options: A class variable is a type of instance variable, and vice versa
A class variable is a variable that belongs to the class, while an instance variable is a variable that belongs to a specific instance of the class
A class variable is a variable that can be accessed from any instance of the class, while an instance variable can only be accessed from the instance it belongs to

questions.text: What is the purpose of the 'super()' function in a Python class method when calling the parent class's method?
options: To call the parent class's method directly
To call the parent class's method indirectly through a proxy object
To bypass the parent class's method and call another method instead
To prevent the parent class's method from being called
questions.explanation: The 'super()' function returns a proxy object that allows calls to methods of a parent class, making it a better practice than calling the parent class's method directly. This ensures that the method resolution order (MRO) is correctly followed.

questions.text: Why does the following code raise a RecursionError when trying to call a method of an instance that has a recursive attribute?
options: The recursive attribute has a circular reference
The instance does not have an __init__ method
The method is not defined for the instance's class
The recursive attribute is not initialized correctly
questions.explanation: A recursive attribute creates a cycle in the object graph, leading to infinite recursion when Python tries to access the attribute. This is because Python's garbage collector does not break cycles, and in this case, the cycle is too deep, causing Python to run out of stack space.

questions.text: Why does the following code raise a NameError when trying to access a private attribute in a parent class from a child class using the 'super()' function?
options: The parent class does not have a private attribute
The child class does not have a private attribute
The 'super()' function cannot access private attributes
The name of the private attribute is not correctly prefixed with a double underscore
questions.explanation: When using the 'super()' function, Python resolves the attribute access through the method resolution order (MRO), but private attributes are prefixed with a double underscore, making them look different in the MRO. As a result, Python does not find the private attribute and raises a NameError.
